catalog_quote: 3. Phonology. The phonology of Dyarim should be regarded as tentative at this stage. ... 3.1 Vowels. Dyarim (probably) has seven phonemic vowels ... All the vowels probably exist in long/short forms although no minimal pairs have been established for some. ... 3.3 Tones. Dyarim Tə has three tone levels phonetically as well as rising and falling tones. ... The basic plural suffix is -sə (as in Guus) which appears to take its tone from the stem vowel. ... Tone-change. Many Dyarim nouns change tones between singular and plural, but for a small subset this is the only change

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: every fragment of the deciding quotation is verbatim in the held Blench 2005 draft text at the stated locator (sect. 3, 3.3 Tones, p. 3) and the key sentence recurs in the scanned of the 2007 published scan we hold (PDF p. 6); 'stress'/'accent' occur nowhere in either version. (2) Deciding source: a first-hand but avowedly tentative 19-page sketch (2005/2007) by the only linguist to have described the language; Glottolog lists no grammar, phonology or sketch for Dyarim, the held Caron South Bauchi papers do not cover it, and the ISO 639-3 change request (downloaded now) adds only lexicostatistics from an SIL survey. So the best available source is held and quoted, but it is thin in absolute terms (one sentence: three phonetic tone levels plus rising/falling contours; morphological tone in plurals), hence 'adequate' rather than 'well-sourced'.
